clue.text: Bottle-opener has inclination to put in stopper

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, so take the start of the word bottle

parts.note: a rake is a slope or inclination, as of a stage or a ship's mast

explanation.surface: A corkscrew seems keen to push a cork into a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle-opener' looks like a corkscrew, but it means only the first letter of 'Bottle', B. Add RAKE, a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake is a device that stops a vehicle or wheel.

clue.text: Reverses promise to supply weapon

parts.note: to back is to reverse, as a car backs
to give one's word is to promise

explanation.surface: Breaking a promise to provide arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A backsword is a sword with a single cutting edge.

clue.text: A range of hearing?

parts.note: the Urals are a mountain range dividing Europe and Asia

explanation.surface: How far can one hear?
explanation.walkthrough: 'range of hearing' reads as earshot; 'range' is the Ural mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Aural means relating to the ear and listening.

clue.text: All made, the day before Roy changed quarters

parts.note: eve is the day before a festival, as Christmas Eve

indicators.note: changed says the letters of the name Roy are rearranged

parts.note: N and E are two compass quarters, north and east

explanation.surface: Everybody pitched in on the day Roy moved house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges ROY to RYO; 'quarters' is compass points, not lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone means every person, the whole lot.

clue.text: A lower tender sought by farmer?

definitions.text: A lower tender sought by farmer?

parts.words: A lower tender sought by farmer?
parts.note: a lower is something that lows, a cow, so a lower tender is someone who looks after cows, a hand a farmer would hire

explanation.surface: A farmer hunts for someone who will put in a cheaper bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower tender' reads as a cheaper bid, but 'lower' is one that lows (a cow) and 'tender' is one who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm hand who tends cows is exactly a person who looks after lowing beasts.

clue.text: Wool applied to ear perhaps?

definitions.meaning: the wool shorn from a flock in one season
a ... round the ear is a light blow, and a ...-on earring fastens to the ear

explanation.surface: Fleece put over the ear, maybe as a muffler.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text's 'car' is an OCR misreading of 'ear'. 'A clip round the ear' is a British phrase for a cuff on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A season's shearing is called the wool clip, and a cuff or a fastener can be put to the ear.

clue.text: Explosive includes a quantity that's equivalent

indicators.note: the explosive includes, that is contains, the next piece

parts.note: TNT is trinitrotoluene, a high explosive
an amount is a quantity

explanation.surface: A bomb packs a measured charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantamount means equal in effect or value.

clue.text: Slips in Bella's composition

indicators.note: composition means putting together, so the letters of the name are put together anew

explanation.surface: Mistakes in a girl's essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' suggests an essay; it signals rearranging BELLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Labels are slips of paper or card fixed to things.

clue.text: Art masters take in the older variety of play

indicators.note: the art masters take in, that is enclose, the scrambled word

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts

indicators.note: a variety of a word is another arrangement of its letters

parts.note: a second MA, Master of Arts, as masters is plural

explanation.surface: Graduates accept an older kind of drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text's '8' is OCR noise. 'Art masters' gives two MAs; the first takes in ELODR, made by 'variety of' from OLDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational play with stock heroes and villains.

clue.text: Poet in two minds apparently

parts.note: being in two minds is wavering between refusal and assent, so the first word is a refusal
the second mind is the word of assent

explanation.surface: A versifier who cannot make up his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Noyes was an English poet, author of The Highwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Noyes wrote the ballad The Highwayman.

clue.text: Ascertain unusual view of a philosopher

indicators.note: an unusual view of a word sees its letters arranged differently

explanation.surface: Find out what a thinker's odd opinion is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual view' signals rearranging the letters of 'Ascertain'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartesian describes the ideas of Descartes, the French philosopher.

clue.text: Perhaps Flashman got — canned?

definitions.meaning: Flashman is the brutal schoolboy tormentor in Tom Brown's Schooldays, an example of a thug who picks on weaker boys
... beef is tinned corned beef, so the word can mean canned

explanation.surface: Did the famous schoolboy rogue get the sack?
explanation.walkthrough: 'canned' suggests sacked; it stands for bully beef, British tinned corned beef. Flashman is the school tormentor in the Victorian novel Tom Brown's Schooldays.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashman is the classic schoolboy tormentor, and bully beef is the tinned corned beef of army rations.

clue.text: Spreads out to get some freedom of movement in vessel

indicators.note: the freedom of movement goes in the vessel, one piece placed within the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel
play is slack or room to move, as in a rope with some play in it

explanation.surface: Someone stretches out to get a little room to move aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To splay is to spread limbs or parts outward.

clue.text: Writes wounding things about a learner composing poems

indicators.note: the wounding things go about, that is around, the other pieces

parts.note: blades are sharp edges that cut and wound
L is the learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A writer pens hurtful lines about a novice while composing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text's 'ems' is an OCR misreading; the page prints 'poems'. 'Writes' and 'composing' only link the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballade is a French verse form of three stanzas and an envoy.

clue.text: Desires transport ?

parts.note: Tennessee Williams's play A Streetcar Named Desire suggests trams named Desire, so desires are kinds of tram

explanation.surface: Longings that carry one away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' reads as rapture; it means vehicles. The play title A Streetcar Named Desire makes 'Desires' the name of trams.
explanation.definitionFit: American trams, after the Tennessee Williams play title.

clue.text: Noise interrupts speech in church ceremony

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle, so the noise sits inside the speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A racket breaks into a sermon during a service.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text's '18' is OCR noise; the page has no number there.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordination is the church rite by which priests are made.

clue.text: Talk of devilled kidneys, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, so a devilled dish is a ..., one course of a meal

explanation.surface: Conversation about spicy offal at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as DIS COURSE: Dis is the underworld god, and devilled kidneys is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is formal speech, and split in two it names a devilish course of a meal.

clue.text: Threads suggest something crooked

definitions.meaning: the lengthwise threads on a loom
to ... is to bend out of shape, and a ... mind is crooked

explanation.surface: Lines of thread hint at a dishonest scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaving terms name the long threads on a loom the warp, and wood that twists out of true is warped, bent.

clue.text: They plunder drink slip up about that

indicators.note: the reversed word goes about, that is around, the drink
in a down clue, up means the word slip is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
lager is a drink

explanation.surface: Looters down a beer and blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SLIP into PILS, which goes 'about' LAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillagers are those who rob by violence, especially in war.

clue.text: Initiated one to Ceres, in strange guise

indicators.note: a strange guise is an odd disguise, so the letters appear rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A newcomer to the cult of the corn goddess in an odd costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in strange guise' rearranges I, TO and CERES. 'Initiated' is an adjective: known only to the initiated.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is meant for or understood by a select inner circle only.

clue.text: One four-letter word in place of another?

definitions.text: One four-letter word in place of another?

parts.words: One four-letter word in place of another?
parts.note: a four-letter word is a swear word; a mild four-letter exclamation is said instead of a stronger one

explanation.surface: A polite term swapped in for a rude one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'four-letter word' means a swear word: this mild word of four letters replaces 'damn', and the punctuation mark of the same name stands in for a deleted oath in print.
explanation.definitionFit: The mild oath and the printed line both substitute for a stronger, censored expletive.

clue.text: Some bounder-in one of the services?-

definitions.text: Some bounder-in one of the services?-

parts.words: Some bounder-in one of the services?-
parts.note: a bounder is a cad, but here it is a thing that bounces; the services are the armed forces, but here a serve in a racket game

explanation.surface: A cad who has joined the army, navy or air force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounder' is old British slang for a cad, and 'services' suggests the armed forces; the thing meant bounces and is used in a serve.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuzzy object that bounces and is struck in every serve of a lawn-court game.

clue.text: Is shelled when port is taken?

definitions.text: Is shelled when port is taken?

parts.words: Is shelled when port is taken?
parts.note: it reads as a harbour under bombardment, but the port is the drink and the shelled thing is a nut cracked open to eat with it

explanation.surface: A harbour town is bombarded when captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelled' and 'port' suggest a naval siege; this nut is shelled and eaten when port wine is drunk after dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The nut traditionally cracked and eaten alongside after-dinner port.

clue.text: Author takes fish without permit

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the fish surrounds the permit

parts.note: a smolt is a young salmon
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A writer goes fishing without a licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking. Tobias Smollett was an 18th-century Scottish novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobias Smollett wrote the novels Roderick Random and Humphry Clinker.

clue.text: Shots of Surrey opener stir the Oval

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter
to stir is to mix, so the letters of Oval are mixed up

explanation.surface: Photos of Surrey's opening batsman stirring up the crowd at the Oval.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground, home of Surrey; 'opener' suggests a batsman, but gives S. 'stir' rearranges OVAL to ALVO.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a burst of simultaneous gunfire.

clue.text: Workers go to a northern island

parts.note: the staff are the people who work for an organisation

explanation.surface: Employees travel to an island in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffa is a small Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides, home of Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is an islet off Mull in the Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Criminal gets cleared by a horse

definitions.meaning: a receiver of stolen goods is a crook
a showjumper or steeplechaser clears a barrier on the course

explanation.surface: A crook is acquitted thanks to a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleared' reads as acquitted; it means jumped.
explanation.definitionFit: A receiver of stolen goods is a criminal, and the barrier a horse jumps is another sense.

clue.text: Grounds or 'pastures, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for pastures is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: leas are meadows or pastures

explanation.surface: Land or fields, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' looks like land, matching 'pastures'; it means the dregs, like coffee grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the sediment at the bottom of a wine vessel, like coffee grounds.

clue.text: Many an old ship is slow in movement

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, standing for many
the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Many an ancient vessel is sluggish in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical marking for a very slow tempo, and a piece's slow section is a largo.

clue.text: Deviation from normal unusually rare? Can be

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the following words appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Something odd can be rare, the clue muses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' signals rearranging RARE, CAN and BE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aberrance is a straying from the usual course or standard.

clue.text: Love poems are about the same — they're too much of a good thing

definitions.text: they're too much of a good thing

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the poems are about, that is around, the other piece

parts.note: verses are poems
do, short for ditto, means the same

explanation.surface: Romantic verses all say the same thing, and become too sickly to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means around: VERSES holds DO, the ditto abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdoses are excessive amounts of a drug, more than is good for one.

clue.text: Miranda's game with Ferdinand

parts.note: in Shakespeare's The Tempest the two lovers are discovered playing a board game together

explanation.surface: What Miranda and Ferdinand played together.
explanation.walkthrough: In Act 5 of The Tempest, Prospero reveals Ferdinand and Miranda at a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game with kings and queens that the Tempest lovers are seen playing.
